crates.name: molla-core
crates.purpose_one_line: The workspace's shared vocabulary: five u32 handle newtypes, one crate-wide error enum, the `Axis` enum, and the `MAXVAL` sentinel — no logic, no dependencies beyond glam/thiserror.
main_modules: src/ids.rs (62 lines: BodyId/ShapeId/JointId/ParticleId/WorldId via id_newtype! macro)
src/error.rs (40 lines: Error enum + Result alias)
crates.note: src/ids.rs:4 doc-links `crate::sim::ModelBuilder::build` — a dangling intra-doc link: molla-core has no `sim` module and cannot depend on molla-sim (that would be a cycle). Stale doc comment referencing another crate's type.

crates.name: molla-math
crates.purpose_one_line: Host-side f64 numerics library for the whole engine: rigid transforms + spatial (6D) algebra, dense 3x3 decompositions, dense and block-sparse and Krylov linear solvers, graph coloring, robust-loss scalars, and a NOAA solar-position model — plus the f32 WGSL-layout mirror structs.
main_modules: src/lib.rs (41 lines: Real/Vec3/Quat/Mat3 aliases, GRAVITY, re-exports)
src/sparse.rs (880: BsrMatrix block-sparse CSR + LinearOperator trait + IterConfig)
src/iterative.rs (649: cg_solve, pcg_solve, bicgstab_solve, JacobiPreconditioner, CgResult)
src/dense3.rs (613: svd3, qr3, eig3_sym, polar_decompose_3 and their adjoints adj_svd3/adj_polar)
src/robust_loss.rs (376: RobustLoss enum + l1/l2_smooth/huber/pseudo_huber/tukey norms and grads)

crates.name: molla-storage
crates.purpose_one_line: One type: `Buffer<T>`, a host/device-mirrored array with a BufferElement trait mapping each host f64 type to its f32 WGSL mirror; the device half exists only under the `gpu` feature.
main_modules: src/buffer.rs (403 lines: BufferUsage, BufferElement trait + 8 impls, Buffer<T> with from_vec/zeros/host/host_mut/ensure_device/upload/download/mark_device_dirty)
crates.note: Whole crate collapses to one 403-line file; the CPU path is fully exercised (3 inline tests at buffer.rs:375+) and needs no GPU.

crates.name: molla-compute
crates.purpose_one_line: wgpu runtime ownership: `Engine` holds Arc<Device>/Arc<Queue> plus Backend selection and AdapterInfo — a thin factory, not a subsystem.
main_modules: src/engine.rs (168 lines: Backend, AdapterInfo, Engine, init_gpu)
crates.note: Everything except the enum/struct shape is behind `#[cfg(feature="gpu")]` in src/lib.rs:3-7; with the feature off the crate exports nothing at all.

crates.name: molla-compute-primitives
crates.purpose_one_line: Seven standalone, self-contained tiled/blocked compute algorithms (radix sort + six `tile_*` primitives), each with a CPU oracle and a feature-gated GPU kernel; currently consumed almost entirely by viewer demos.
main_modules: src/tile_mcgp.rs (138: mcgp_estimate SPSA estimator, McgpConfig, finite_diff_central)

crates.name: molla-optim
crates.purpose_one_line: Two first-order host optimizers over flat f64 slices — Adam/AdamW and SGD with momentum/Nesterov/weight-decay — as plain state structs mirroring Warp's wp.optim.
main_modules: src/lib.rs (52 lines: large math doc-comment + re-exports)
crates.note: src/lib.rs:11-19 claims GPU dispatch lives in `crate::kernels::optim_{adam,sgd}` — false from inside molla-optim (it has no kernels module and only depends on molla-math). The real GPU dispatchers are in molla-kernels. Stale doc cross-reference.

crates.name: molla-autograd
crates.purpose_one_line: CPU-only reverse-mode differentiation: a generic op Tape plus five hand-written closed-form adjoints (Featherstone ABA, MPM, XPBD, Stam fluid, 2-link arm) — the largest crate in the region at 8087 loc, almost all of it numeric adjoint math.
main_modules: src/lib.rs (30 lines: `pub use molla_math as math` + re-exports)
src/tape.rs (749: Tape, TapeId, TapeOp, TapeCheckpoint — 5 op variants Add/Sub/Mul/MatVec/Norm)
src/featherstone_adjoint.rs (2416: FeatherstoneRevoluteChain, JacobianStrategy, JacobianScratch, JointKind, record_featherstone_step)
src/mpm_cpu_diff.rs (774: forward pass + tape for MPM)
tests/ (7 files: featherstone x3, xpbd, mpm_diff_optim, probe_cpu_diff, stam_diff)

connection_health.summary: The region is a correct, well-documented, heavily-commented numerical core with a healthy low-level spine (core -> math -> storage -> compute/compute-primitives -> optim/autograd) and a badly frayed top layer where every interesting capability is reachable only through the viewer demo binary or through a facade shim.
healthy: molla-core -> molla-math -> molla-storage is a clean acyclic spine; molla-storage is the single point where f64 becomes f32 and it does exactly that job (buffer.rs:40-120 BufferElement impls).

molla-math is genuinely load-bearing across the workspace: 581 `molla_math::` tokens, with sparse/iterative reaching molla-fem (55/49/31/... uses per file) and spatial/transform reaching molla-sim. It is the one crate in the region that is clearly not disposable.
molla-compute's Engine is used by 174 token sites across molla-geometry and molla-kernels — the GPU runtime abstraction is real and central.
Every crate in the region is independently buildable as a leaf: molla-optim depends only on molla-math; molla-autograd only on molla-math.
frayed: molla-optim has NO production consumer of its optimizer behaviour: the only non-test, non-facade callers read `AdamConfig`/`SgdConfig` as plain data in molla-kernels' GPU dispatchers (optim_adam.rs:14, optim_sgd.rs:10). `AdamState::step`/`SgdState::step` — the actual algorithms, and the whole 540-loc crate's reason to exist — are called only from tests (molla-fem tests x3, molla-kernels tests x2, molla-autograd tests x2, molla-solvers tests x1).

molla-autograd's genuinely-used surface is narrow: `DiffArm` (viewer examples 10/18/19 + crates/molla/examples/diff_arm_reach.rs + crates/molla/tests/scene_smoke.rs), `FeatherstoneRevoluteChain` (molla-kernels/src/featherstone_adjoint.rs, molla-solvers/src/featherstone.rs), `JacobianScratch`/`JacobianStrategy` (molla-kernels), and `Tape` (3 files). The MPM and Stam halves are unreachable from workspace code.
molla-compute-primitives' tile_* family is reachable only from viewer examples; the only engine consumer is radix_sort (molla-geometry/src/lbvh.rs:51,133,314,337 and molla-kernels/src/tire_dem.rs).

Two 1000+ loc crates (compute-primitives, autograd) route most of their public surface through `crates/molla/src/compute/*.rs` and `crates/molla/src/autograd/*.rs` wrappers, which obscures who actually calls what: a naive `grep molla_compute_primitives::` returns 23, but the real path is `molla::compute::tile_*`.
connection_health.cycles: No crate-level dependency cycles in the region. At the namespace level molla-kernels and molla-solvers cross-export (solvers -> kernels -> compute, plus solvers re-exports kernels and molla-kernels re-exports compute), which is one-directional in Cargo but reads as a tangle in source.
connection_health.note_on_grep: A zero `grep -rn "molla_<name>::"` count is NOT proof of an unused dependency in this workspace because of the `as` alias pattern (crates/molla-kernels/src/lib.rs:3-7, crates/molla-solvers/src/lib.rs:7-18, crates/molla-autograd/src/lib.rs:7). Any automated removal pass must follow `crate::math::`, `crate::core::`, `crate::autograd::` too.
